The Prophet forbade two ways of wearing a garment, Ishtimal As-Samma and Ihtiba leaving the private parts uncovered, and two bargains, Mulamasa and Munabadha.
Fatima wept when the Prophet confided that his death was near and laughed when told she would be chief of the believing women, telling Aisha only after his death.
The Prophet was seen lying on his back in the mosque with one leg over the other.
Two should not talk secretly apart from a third; Anas kept the Prophet's secret, Ibn Mas'ud secretly reported an angering remark, and one man's private talk outlasted the iqama.
At bedtime put out fires and lamps, close the doors and cover vessels and food, for fire burnt a house in Medina and a rat may drag a wick.
Five things are of the fitra, circumcision among them; Abraham circumcised himself past eighty, and Ibn Abbas was already circumcised when the Prophet died, boys then being circumcised at puberty.
Whoever swears by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza should say none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and whoever invites a friend to gamble should give something in charity.
Ibn Umar built a house with his own hands in the Prophet's lifetime and said he built and planted nothing after the Prophet died, though a relative disputed it.
Every prophet has one invocation that is answered, and the Prophet keeps his to intercede for his followers on the Day of Resurrection.
The best plea for forgiveness, said with faith, brings Paradise to one dying that day or night; the Prophet repented over seventy times daily, and Allah rejoices greatly at repentance.
At bedtime the Prophet lay on his right side with words of surrender, recited the Mu'awwidhat and taught glorifications, and when praying at night asked for light and forgiveness.
In the last third of every night the Lord descends to the nearest heaven, asking who will invoke Him, ask Him or seek His forgiveness, that He may answer.
On going to the lavatory the Prophet sought refuge with Allah from al-khubuth and al-khaba'ith.
The Prophet gave the best plea for forgiveness, said 'In Your name I die and live' at bedtime and taught prayer invocations; invocation should be neither loud nor low.
The poor were told glorifying, praising and magnifying Allah ten times each after every prayer would match the rich, and the Prophet declared Allah's oneness after each prayer.
The Prophet invoked mercy and blessing on Amir at Khaibar, those bringing alms, Jarir sent against Dhul-Khalasa, Anas, a reciter who reminded him of a verse, and Moses.
Avoid rhymed prose in invocation and preach sparingly; ask Allah with determination, not 'if You wish', without growing impatient; the Prophet raised his hands until his armpits showed.
Asked in a Friday sermon, the Prophet invoked rain, then after a week's downpour asked that it fall around them; praying for rain at the Musalla, he turned his cloak.
The Prophet prayed for Anas's wealth and children, declared Allah's oneness, Lord of the Throne, in distress, and sought refuge from calamity, an evil end and enemies' gloating.
No prophet dies before being shown his place in Paradise and given the choice, and the Prophet's last words, his head on Aisha's thigh, were 'O Allah, the Highest Companions'.
Khabbab, branded seven times, would have prayed for death but for the Prophet's ban; none should long for death over a calamity but ask to live while life is better.

The Prophet blessed children, stroking As-Sa'ib's head, pouring water on an infant's urine, spraying Mahmud's face, touching another's eye; men sought partnership with Abdullah bin Hisham, whom he blessed.
Asked how to send Salat on him, the Prophet taught 'O Allah, send Salat on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham's family', and invoked Salat on those bringing alms.
The Prophet asked Allah to make any abuse of his against a believer a means of bringing that believer near to Him on the Day of Resurrection.
Angered by many questions, the Prophet offered to answer any; a man learned his father was Hudhaifa, Umar sought refuge from afflictions, and Paradise and Hell were shown to him.

The Prophet sought refuge from worry, grief, incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, debt, old age, worldly affliction and the grave's punishment, which he confirmed after Aisha doubted two Jewish women.
The Prophet asked Allah to make them love Medina as much as Mecca or more, move its fever to Al-Juhfa, and bless their measures.
Gravely ill, Sa'd was told even a third in charity is too much, since leaving heirs rich is better, and the Prophet prayed his companions' emigration be completed.
The Prophet sought refuge from cowardice, miserliness, old age, the trial and punishment of grave and Fire, poverty, wealth and the Dajjal, asking that his sins be washed away.
Um Sulaim asked the Prophet to invoke blessing for Anas, his servant, and he asked Allah to increase his wealth and offspring and bless what He gave him.
The Prophet taught the Istikhara: two voluntary rak'at, then asking Allah by His knowledge and power to decree a matter if good and turn it away if bad.
After ablution the Prophet raised his hands and asked Allah to forgive Ubaid Abi Amir and raise him above many on the Day of Resurrection.
Shouting Takbir is needless, for Allah hears and sees; 'La haula wala quwwata illa billah' is a treasure of Paradise; the Prophet praised Allah on heights and returning from journeys.
The Prophet invoked blessing on the marriages of Abdur-Rahman bin Auf and Jabir, and taught a husband words seeking protection from Satan before intercourse, protecting any child conceived.
The Prophet's most frequent invocation asked for good in this world and the Hereafter and safety from the Fire; he taught refuge from miserliness, cowardice, old age and worldly affliction.
Bewitched by Labid bin Al-A'sam so he thought he had done what he had not, the Prophet invoked Allah, learned from two men where the spell lay, and was cured.
The Prophet invoked against the confederates, Mudar, Usaiya and those who made him miss Asr at the Trench, returned the Jews' greeting in kind, but prayed for Daus's guidance.
The Prophet asked Allah to forgive his mistakes, ignorance and excess, his jest and earnest, what he did deliberately or not, past and future, secret and open.
On Friday there is a brief time when Allah grants whatever good a Muslim who is praying asks of Him.
When Jews wished the Prophet death and Aisha cursed them, he urged gentleness, saying he had returned their words and his invocation against them is accepted, theirs not.
